clue.text: Hound dame nicely performing this?

indicators.note: performing suggests the three words are put through their paces and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer imagines which song would let them charm a hound and a dame at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the song is what you get when 'Hound dame nicely' is performed, that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known love song, famously sung by the Righteous Brothers, is the piece a performer would sing here.

clue.text: Some sure sir, pushy, climbing?

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
Some says only part of the run of words that follows is wanted

explanation.surface: A pushy man, sure of himself, is on his way up the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks letters out of 'sure sir, pushy'; 'climbing' turns them round. The whole clue also describes the answer: a pushy social climber.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises up, especially socially, is exactly what a pushy, climbing person is.

clue.text: Smoke in vehicle — serviceman upset

indicators.note: in places the turned soldier inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier, annoyed, lights up while sitting in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning something to smoke; a rolled tobacco leaf is a classic example.

clue.text: Tough para's unusual signature

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A hard paratrooper has a distinctive way of signing his name.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'para' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a person's handwritten name, especially one asked for by fans.

clue.text: 12 either way

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards as backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.walkthrough: Twelve o'clock midday is the definition; the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday falls at twelve o'clock, so the number stands for that hour.

clue.text: Tactful individual, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: individual means separate, distinct

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a tactful individual, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: careful not to cause offence or reveal secrets.

clue.text: Precise European times performance

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A punctual continental keeps careful time for each show.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: accurate in every detail, correct.

clue.text: Exotic rose I found (with no name) having fragrant scent

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged
with no says a letter is dropped from the word beside it

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an unnamed foreign rose with a lovely smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no name' takes N from 'found', leaving FOUD; this joins ROSE and I before 'Exotic' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: giving off a smell, usually a pleasant one.

clue.text: New style home — Russian

indicators.note: new says the letters come out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A fresh design for a house in the Russian manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Boris, the first President of post-Soviet Russia.

clue.text: Morally justifiable trick? Strange ethos — round the bend!

parts.note: to rig is to fix or trick

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the next piece
strange says the letters are oddly ordered

parts.note: U stands for a U-shaped bend, as in U-bend

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a con is justified, with a peculiar morality that seems mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns ETHOS into HTEOS, which goes 'round' U to make HTEOUS. 'round the bend' looks like slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: virtuous, in the right by moral standards.

clue.text: Marie loves hugging gazelle

indicators.note: hugging says the letters are held inside the words around them

explanation.surface: A woman called Marie cuddles a small antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Arabian gazelle of that name.

clue.text: Quiet sport gets empty gestures

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A sport played quietly yields only hollow signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural noun: lifts of the shoulders signalling indifference.

clue.text: Fusses about Royal relatives

indicators.note: about places the first word around the letter that follows

parts.note: to bother is to fuss

explanation.surface: People make a fuss about the relatives of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Male siblings are relatives, sharing the same parents.

clue.text: Daily with short country coat

parts.note: a rag is a newspaper, and a daily is a newspaper

indicators.note: short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a land is a country

explanation.surface: A cleaner wears a cut-down overcoat from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a cleaning lady (British slang) but is a daily newspaper, a rag.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an overcoat with sleeves running to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: One refusing to give thanks after energy comes to current price

indicators.note: after puts the ungrateful one behind the energy

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
an ingrate is an ungrateful person

explanation.surface: An ungrateful man finally gets going and asks what things cost now.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the usual charge being paid at present for a thing.

clue.text: New — a one-stop sugar supplier?

indicators.note: new says the letters are given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new one-stop shop opens selling sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a small piece of cutlery used to put sugar into tea.

clue.text: Some coal maybe in Southern shack — fuel lacking effectiveness originally

parts.note: a hovel is a shack

indicators.note: lacking says a letter goes from the word before it
originally points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: In a Southern shack, the coal burns poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives E, which 'lacking' removes from FUEL to leave FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity held on a spade; coal is one example of what it might hold.

clue.text: Hot English women tying the knot somewhere in Scotland?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
brides are women getting married

explanation.surface: Passionate English brides head north for a Scottish wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The island groups off Scotland's west coast; the question mark marks the vague location.

clue.text: Become more intense, hard — this clue has letter missing?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: has letter missing says one letter is dropped from the number

parts.note: this clue is numbered 18

explanation.surface: A difficult clue gets harder because a letter seems to be absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue' is 18-across, so the number spelt out is used, with one E dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to increase or intensify, as tension does.

clue.text: Initially hearing reservations, your view now is accepted — money needed in Kiev

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Reservations are heard and your view is now accepted, with cash required in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Ukraine, whose capital is Kiev (Kyiv).

clue.text: Mugs possible England boss?

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them
on means feasible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Muggings carried out by a would-be England manager.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Bobby, who managed the England football team; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: African leader in New York before queen turns up

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An African statesman visits New York before the Queen arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius, first president of Tanzania, is an example of an African leader.

clue.text: Roy ought to change milk-based food

indicators.note: change says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Roy should alter his diet of dairy food.
explanation.definitionFit: A fermented dairy product made by adding bacteria to milk; this is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Regularly visited port (Rangoon) and NZ region

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A traveller often called at the port of Rangoon and a New Zealand region.
explanation.definitionFit: A region in New Zealand's South Island, containing Dunedin.

clue.text: Man from Paris I brought to Italian city

parts.note: je is French for I
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: A Frenchman takes himself off to an Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a man's first name, as in the author of Three Men in a Boat.

clue.text: Arab shortly rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: in a mo means shortly, in a moment

explanation.surface: An Arab is getting up in a minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Oman, an Arab country, is an example of an Arab.

clue.text: Some info cited centres of attention

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the cited information is where interest gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural noun: the points on which interest or activity concentrates.

clue.text: Irish girl back in Kampala unexpectedly

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Irish girl turns up back in Uganda's capital by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the hiding signal: ALAUN sits across 'Kampala unexpectedly' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an Irish female first name.

clue.text: Cross about blemish returning in metal entrance feature

indicators.note: about says the word is turned around

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, a cross

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the metal's symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a metal

indicators.note: returning says the word is read backwards

parts.note: to mar is to blemish

explanation.surface: Someone angry at a mark coming back on metal at the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is a crucifix; 'about' and 'returning' each turn their word round.
explanation.definitionFit: The fixed surround of a doorway is a structural part of an entrance.

clue.text: Question about relationship put another way — same routine, Lily?

indicators.note: put another way says the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks Lily, in different words, whether the relationship is still the same old routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover's anxious query about whether the partner still belongs to them; also a song title.
